name: How do I know if my bathroom has hidden water damage before remodeling?

mainEntity.name: What signs suggest a bathroom may have hidden water damage or rot before demolition starts?
mainEntity.text: What signs suggest a bathroom may have hidden water damage or rot before demolition starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden water damage is one of the biggest risks in a bathroom remodel. Warning signs include loose or hollow-feeling tile, a soft or uneven floor, recurring grout cracks, discoloration around the shower, bubbling paint, and a mildew smell that never fully goes away. Water may also travel into adjacent rooms or the ceiling below. If the bathroom has older plumbing or a shower that has never been properly waterproofed, the chances of concealed damage are higher. Before choosing finishes, homeowners should ask for a thorough inspection and be prepared for exploratory demolition if the room is older. A contractor should explain how discoveries will be documented, priced, and repaired so the project does not stall unexpectedly once the walls are open.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common signs of hidden water damage include soft flooring, cracked grout, loose tile, peeling paint, musty odors, swelling around baseboards, and stains on ceilings below the bathroom. Even if the surface looks fine, damage can exist behind walls or under the subfloor until demolition reveals it.
